judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under Curricular Goal CG-4 (measuring attributes with standard and non-standard units, relating measure and number). The first (Class-3, rank 2, under C-4.1 'Measures using both non-standard and standard units and understands the importance of standard units') is 'Need for standard measurements', with LC 'Understand the need for standard units of measurement'. The second (Class-4, rank 3, under C-4.3 on unit conversion and everyday problems) is 'Measurement-related application problems using addition and subtraction', with LCs solving measurement application problems by addition and by subtraction. Direction is lower-to-higher rank and substantive rather than mere repetition: grasping why standard units are needed is what makes measures commensurable quantities that can be added and subtracted in application problems, so the Class-3 conceptual understanding supports success in the Class-4 computational application. Shared 'measurement' tokens and same-page proximity alone were not treated as evidence; the judgment rests on the statement and LC texts. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 Content bullets (rank 4, identical coordinate) under the same Competency C-2.5 'Identifies, describes and extends simple number patterns, including odd and even numbers, square and triangular numbers'. The first covers 'Patterns in division- Dividing by 10 and 100' (LCs: identify patterns in division when dividing by 10 / by 100); the second covers 'Square and triangular numbers' (LCs: identify, describe and extend patterns of square and of triangular numbers). They are complementary instantiations of the same pattern-recognition competency at the same class level, giving substantive topical coherence around identifying and extending number patterns. However, the evidence shows no substantive dependency: place-value division patterns and figurate (square/triangular) numbers are mathematically distinct strands, neither being a prerequisite for or an extension of the other, and same-rank direction would require substantive evidence that is absent (overlap is limited to the generic token 'patterns'/'numbers' and same page/row provenance). Hence symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards.

The second SFI is Class-1 'Addition (sum not exceeding 20)' (LC: 'Add numbers with sum not exceeding 20', rank 0); the first is Class-2 'Subtraction (up to 99)' (LC: 'Develop and use strategies for subtraction of numbers up to 99', rank 1). producer_judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-4.4 'Develops strategies to estimate time' (CG-4 measurement), with resolved Class coordinates Class-4 (rank 3) and Class-5 (rank 4), so only lower-to-higher direction is permitted. The Class-4 item establishes clock-time convention knowledge ('A.M and P.M'; LC: distinguish a.m./p.m. to identify the time of day), while the Class-5 item applies time to daily-life word problems using multiplication and division (LCs: solve time problems in daily-life contexts using multiplication; using division). This is substantive extension within the same time-measurement thread rather than generic repetition: secure reading/interpretation of time-of-day notation plausibly supports success in reasoning about and computing with times in real-life contexts. Confidence is moderated because the Class-5 target also depends heavily on multiplication/division operations not evidenced by the Class-4 item, and both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 and 33 omitted items), so the shared-topic linkage rests on the bounded excerpts and LCs supplied.
